passage: Archaeologists studying early human settlements have recently uncovered evidence suggesting that trade networks developed far earlier than previously believed. Excavations at inland sites revealed shells, minerals, and crafted objects originating from coastal regions hundreds of miles away. These findings challenge the idea that prehistoric communities were isolated and self-sufficient. Instead, they indicate that groups exchanged goods over considerable distances, likely through a chain of intermediary communities. Although the exact motivations behind these exchanges are not fully understood, researchers believe that early trade served both practical and social functions. Items such as pigments and decorative shells may have held symbolic value used in rituals or social ceremonies. The discovery reshapes our understanding of prehistoric society, revealing a level of cooperation and connection that predates the rise of formal civilizations.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.A: Early humans avoided long-distance interaction due to environmental barriers.
choices.B: New evidence suggests prehistoric groups engaged in extensive trade networks.
choices.C: Archaeologists have proven that all prehistoric trade was strictly ceremonial.
choices.D: Coastal communities were more advanced than inland settlements.

questions.explanation: The passage centers on evidence showing early trade occurred across long distances.
